land.text: the Wanyan Jurchens' country round the Ashi river and Huanglong, subjects of the Khitan-led Liao until 1114

predecessors.note: 'Starting in 1114, Aguda united the Jurchen tribes under his rule and rebelled against the Liao dynasty' (Wanyan Aguda page); infobox 'Founded by Aguda: 28 January 1115'. The Liao lost the rest of its land to the Jin in 1115-1125 (see the liao-dynasty dossier).

land.text: North China annexed by the Mongols with the fall of Caizhou on 9 February 1234 (Henan, Shaanxi and the remnant; Hebei, Shanxi and Shandong had passed to them by 1223)

successors.note: Jin page infobox successors: Mongol Empire, Southern Song (Tangzhou and Dengzhou, parts of Henan 1233), Qara Khitai, Eastern Xia and Eastern Liao (the Manchurian and Khitan successor states of 1212-1216).

capitals.name: Huiningfu (Shangjing, Acheng near Harbin)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Huiningfu (1122-1153)'; the page calls Huining the Supreme Capital. Before 1122 the pages give no seat; Aguda's home was on the Ashi river (Harbin).

capitals.name: Zhongdu (Yanjing, Beijing)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Zhongdu (1153-1214)'; the body: 'In 1152, Liang relocated his residence to Yanjing and renamed it the Central Capital'. Xuanzong left on 27 June 1214 (Emperor Xuanzong page); the city fell on 1 June 1215.

capitals.name: Kaifeng (Bianjing, the Southern Capital)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Kaifeng (1214-1233)'; 'on 27 June [1214], Emperor Xuanzong left Zhongdu and moved the Jin capital southward to Bianjing'; Aizong fled it towards the end of 1232 (Emperor Aizong page).

capitals.name: Caizhou (Runan)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Caizhou (1233-1234)'; Aizong hanged himself there as the Mongols and Song stormed it on 9 February 1234.

rulers.name: Taizu (Wanyan Aguda)
rulers.note: Proclaimed the Jin in January 1115 (infobox 28 January); died August or 19 September 1123 (Wanyan Aguda page).

rulers.name: Taizong (Wanyan Wuqimai)
rulers.note: Page: succeeded Aguda in 1123 and died in 1135.

rulers.name: Hailing (Wanyan Liang)
rulers.note: Murdered on 15 December 1161; the page gives no reign years.

rulers.name: Shizong (Wanyan Wulu)
rulers.note: Crowned at Liaoyang on 27 October 1161; died in 1189.

rulers.name: Wanyan Yongji (Shaowang)
rulers.note: Succeeded Zhangzong; 'assassinated in the eighth month of 1213' (Xuanzong page); no reign dates on the pages.

rulers.name: Aizong (Wanyan Shouxu)
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 15 January 1224 - 9 February 1234'; hanged himself at Caizhou.

rulers.name: Mo (Wanyan Chenglin)
rulers.note: Infobox lists 'Modi' with the date 1234; 'ruled for less than a day before he was finally killed in battle' (Mongol conquest page).

'The area was later conquered by the Jin dynasty (1115-1234), which ceded the area to the Western Xia in 1136' (re-opened; the Jin page says nothing of it). Region as in the western-xia dossier (Xining, 100 km). Added after review; the Jin page lists no earlier conquest of it, so it is read as part of the 1130 gain.

1139: the Jin hand back Henan and Shaanxi.

ledger.note: 1139: the Linxia and Lanzhou discs leave the Jin shape. Cliopatria's Great Jin shape of 1139 holds neither (nor does its Western Xia or Southern Song shape) and no page opened says who held them after the Jin; the loss to nobody bridges that silence (confidence 1). Added after review.
1140: the Jin retake the plain. 'In 1140, the Jin retook Shaanxi and Henan'; 'On July 8, 1140, at the Battle of Yancheng, Wuzhu launched a surprise attack on Song forces' (Jin-Song wars page).
1140: Henan and Shaanxi are Jin again.
11 October 1142: the Treaty of Shaoxing. 'A peace treaty with the Song was finalized on 11 October 1142' (Jin page); the Huai river was the border; the treaty ceded Tangzhou and Dengzhou.

region.text: the lands north of the Qinling-Huai line, including Kaifeng

ledger.note: 1142: the Song renounce the north. They gave up claims to lands 'north of the Qinling Huaihe Line, which included its former capital of Kaifeng'.
1142: the Song pay tribute. 250,000 taels of silver and 250,000 packs of silk yearly to 'the suzerain Jin'; the Gaozong page: the Song were 'a vassal state to the Jin'.
1153: the capital moves to Zhongdu. Infobox 'Zhongdu (1153-1214)'; the body says Wanyan Liang relocated to Yanjing 'in 1152'.
October 1161: Wanyan Liang crosses the Huai (28 October), loses at Tangdao (16 November) and Caishi (26-27 November) and is murdered on 15 December; Shizong was crowned at Liaoyang on 27 October.
1165: the Treaty of Longxing ends the war (Jin page); the Jin-Song wars page: hostilities 'subsided in 1165 after the negotiation of a peace treaty'.
1165: the tribute lapses. The Treaty of Shaoxing page: tribute 'until 1164, when Jin launched a further war'; the 1165 settlement is the page's peace.
1206: the Song declare war (14 June 1206); 'by the fall of 1206, multiple towns and military bases had been captured by the Jurchens' (Zhangzong page).
2 November 1208: peace; the Song tribute to the Jin is reinstated (50,000 taels of silver and 50,000 packs of fabric).
1208: the Song are tributaries again ('the Song tribute to the Jin was reinstated').

1210: the Xia break with the Jin. 'In 1210, Western Xia attacked the Jin dynasty as punishment for their refusal to aid them against the Mongols' after Xiangzong submitted to the Mongols in January 1210.

region.text: the northern frontier at the Great Wall: Wushabao, Yehuling, Huihebao

ledger.note: 1211: the Mongols invade. 'In 1211, Mongol troops broke through the Jin's Great Wall at Wushabao and attacked fortresses along the border'; the Jin general Wanyan Jiujin failed to attack at Yehuling.

region.text: Liaodong, held by the Khitan rebel Yelu Liuge

ledger.note: 1212: the Khitans rebel. 'In 1212, the Khitan leader Yelu Liuge rebelled against the Jin and declared his allegiance to Genghis Khan.' The page does not name Liaodong; the land is the reading.
27 June 1214: Xuanzong leaves Zhongdu for Bianjing (Kaifeng), 'above the objections of many courtiers' (Mongol conquest page).

1215: Manchuria goes to Puxian Wannu. 'Established in Manchuria (including Northeast China and Outer Manchuria) by the Jurchen warlord Puxian Wannu in 1215' (Eastern Xia page); the Xuanzong page: 'the warlord Puxian Wannu rebelled against the Jin dynasty' (year not stated) and 'declared himself king of the Eastern Xia regime in Liaodong'. Cliopatria drops Manchuria in 1216. The Jin page lists Eastern Xia as a successor.

union.text: Manchuria

region.text: Zhongdu and northern Hebei above 39.8 N

ledger.note: 1 June 1215: Zhongdu falls. 'Zhongdu fell to the Mongols on June 1, 1215' (the Xuanzong page has 31 May).

1223: the northern provinces are lost. Mukhali 'systematically rooted out all resistance in Shanxi, Hebei and Shandong' in 1217-1223; in 1223 he struck into Shaanxi and besieged Feng County, then died of illness.
1231: Shaanxi is lost. 'In 1231, the Mongols attacked again and finally took Fengxiang' after the Jin success at Tong Pass in 1230.
1233: the court flees to Caizhou. 'Towards the end of 1232, Emperor Aizong fled Bianjing' after the Mongols defeated the Jin at Sanfengshan in 1232 and besieged the city.

region.text: Henan except the upper Huai valley round Caizhou

ledger.note: 1233: Kaifeng and Henan pass to the Mongols. The page does not date the fall of Kaifeng ('by this time Kaifeng had been taken'); the Song, allied with the Mongols from 1233, got 'parts of Henan' in return for supplies.
1233: the Song ally with the Mongols against the Jin. The page does not date an end to the tribute; the alliance of 1233 ends the relation in practice.

region.text: the Yellow River plain and Shaanxi fought over by Jin, Song and Jin's puppets

ledger.note: 9 February 1234: the Mongol-Jin war ends at Caizhou. 'Thus the Jin dynasty came to an end on February 9, 1234.'
1234: the Jin end and with them the Goryeo tribute (Cliopatria's Goryeo allegiance row runs to 1235).

region.text: the last Jin land: the upper Huai valley round Caizhou

ledger.note: 9 February 1234: Aizong hangs himself at Caizhou. 'On 9 February 1234, the allied forces of the Mongols and Southern Song dynasty' stormed the city; Emperor Mo, Wanyan Chenglin, 'was killed in action'.

wars.outcome: Hebei and Shanxi taken in 1126, Kaifeng on 9 January 1127; the Jin puppets Chu (1127) and Qi (1130-1137); the raid on the Yangtze delta of December 1129-February 1130; Henan and Shaanxi returned in 1139 and retaken in 1140; the Treaty of Shaoxing (ratified 11 October 1142) fixes the Huai-Qinling border and makes the Song a tributary.

wars.name: Jin-Song war of 1161
wars.outcome: Wanyan Liang's invasion crossed the Huai on 28 October 1161, lost at Tangdao and Caishi and ended with his murder on 15 December; the Treaty of Longxing, 1165.

wars.name: Jin-Song war of 1206-1208
wars.outcome: The Song declared war on 14 June 1206 and lost; peace on 2 November 1208 with the Song tribute reinstated.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty
wars.outcome: Invasion of 1211, Khitan revolt 1212, the move to Kaifeng 1214, Zhongdu 1 June 1215, Mukhali's clearing of Hebei, Shanxi and Shandong 1217-1223, Shaanxi 1230-1231, Sanfengshan 1232, Kaifeng 1232-1233 and Caizhou on 9 February 1234.
wars.note: The Xuanzong page has a Jin-Song war of 1217-1224 and a break with Western Xia, both undated there.

wars.name: Jin-Xia relations and the war of 1210
wars.outcome: Xia attacked the Jin in 1210 after submitting to the Mongols and joined them against the Jin in 1211; Xuanzong 'severed ties' with Western Xia (undated).

certainty.note: The conquest fronts of 1115-1125 and the moving Yellow River-Huai front are approximate.
The Huai-Qinling border with the Song was fixed by the Treaty of Shaoxing (ratified 11 October 1142) and renewed in 1165 and 1208; the northern and western frontiers stay soft.
The Mongol war front changed year by year; the 1223, 1231 and 1233 shapes are approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria's Great Jin starts in 1126 but the dynasty was founded in January 1115 and had the Liao by 1125: five new keyframes (1115, 1120, 1122, 1123, 1125) follow the Jin page's dated captures of the Liao capitals. The Jin shapes of 1126-1138 omit Hebei and Shanxi, the 1139 shape starts a year early for the 1140 retaking, and the 1216/1227 shapes (784 thousand km2) stay unchanged for 1215-1235 although the Mongols took Hebei, Shanxi and Shandong by 1223, Shaanxi by 1231 and everything but Caizhou by 1233; the Jin ended on 9 February 1234, not 1235. The infobox area (3.61 M km2 for 1142; 4.75 M km2 for 1186) is 1.7 to 2.2 times Cliopatria's 2.12 M km2; the shape is kept and the infobox taken to include the tribal sphere.

Not settled: the extent of Zhang Bangchang's Chu (March 1127, one month) and of Liu Yu's Qi (1130-1137) is not on the pages (Henan and Shandong are the reading); Great Chu, Great Qi, Eastern Liao (Yelu Liuge, 1213-1219), Eastern Xia (Puxian Wannu, 1215-1233) and Northern Liao need dossiers; the Song tribute episodes (1142-1165, 1208-1233) are recorded as vassal events because Cliopatria's allegiance row says so, but the Treaty of Shaoxing page itself calls the Song a 'quasi-tributary state'; the pages do not give the year the 1208 tribute stopped; the Dongjing (Liaoyang) capture, the fall of Kaifeng and the Jin-Xia war of 1214-1224 are undated on the pages opened; Shaanxi's loss is dated only by Fengxiang in 1231 (confidence 2). The Jin ceded the Qingtang area to Western Xia in 1136 (Tsongkha page) but that area is outside Cliopatria's Jin shape. Cliopatria shape 1126 reaches Primorye and the Amur; no page opened gives the northern frontier. Name needed in the gazetteer: none.

Fix round after review (2026-10-19): the Jin now gain the land north of the Qinling-Huai line from the Song in 1130 (same region spec as the northern-song loss: the Song's 1126-1129 shape minus Cliopatria's 1139 Southern Song shape) and split Qi's plain (the great-qi founding region) from it; keyframes great-jin_1130 (1130-1135) and great-jin_1136 hold the rest, great-jin_1137 holds all of it; the 145 thousand grid-km2 step of the 1139 keyframes is explained. The Xining disc passes to Western Xia in 1136 (Tsongkha page). The Linxia and Lanzhou discs leave the Jin shape in 1139 with no page (loss to nobody, confidence 1); this is the open gap. great-jin_1227 is marked wrong with the 1223 shape as its correction. Not done here: the great-qi dossier still gives Qi the plain only; the vassal region (Henan, Shandong) is not the same spec as the split region (the plain minus the Southern Song 1139 shape).
